heroHeadline: Lebanon–Israel Ceasefire Collapses in Practice: IDF Chief Declares 'No Effective Cessation of Hostilities' as 9 Killed in Apr 30 Strikes
heroSubtitle: IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir's April 30 declaration that there is 'no effective cessation of hostilities' with Hezbollah marks the de facto end of the three-week ceasefire extension secured in Washington on April 23. At least nine Lebanese were killed by Israeli strikes on April 30 alone, with more than 20 killed in the preceding 24 hours — including Lebanese army soldiers and paramedics — as Israel continues to demolish homes and conduct operations beyond the agreed buffer zone. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun condemned 'continuing Israeli violations' and PM Nawaf Salam reiterated that full Israeli withdrawal under UNSC Resolution 1701 remains a non-negotiable condition. Hezbollah has declared the ceasefire 'meaningless' and continues to launch drones and rockets. Total Lebanese deaths since hostilities resumed March 2 have surpassed 2,500. Separately, the UN Security Council held a private meeting on Myanmar on April 30 as the SAC's self-declared ceasefire expired and resistance groups continued to reject the junta's 100-day peace offer. Ten ceasefire frameworks remain nominally in force globally, with Lebanon, Gaza, and DRC-Rwanda all facing acute implementation crises.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
